# Part 2: Genome assembly

## Assemble a genome using Pacbio HiFi reads


1. On HPC3, download the reads from [/data/class/ee282/public/ISO1\_Hifi\_AdaptorRem.40X.fasta.gz](https://hpc.oit.uci.edu/~solarese/ee282/iso1_onp_a2_1kb.fastq.gz).  
2. Use hifiasm to assemble reads. Use sbatch

**Note**: As is frequently the case, hifiasm  is available on [bioconda](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/hifiasm/README.html)

[Links to an external site.](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/hifiasm/README.html)

**Hints:**  You will need to run the assembly command with more threads (16). [Modify](https://rcic.uci.edu/slurm/jobs.html#interactive-job) the srun command to request for more cores/threads.  It will take \~45 minutes to run with 16 threads. Be patient. You will also need to convert the gfa file to a fasta file. See [documentation.](https://github.com/chhylp123/hifiasm?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started)

[Links to an external site.](https://github.com/chhylp123/hifiasm?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started)

Treat assembly from \*.bp.p\_ctg.gfa  as your main assembly going forward.


```shell
#using hifi to assemble the genome

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $mamba activate ee282
(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $conda install bioconda::hifiasm
#Retrieving notices: done
#Proceed ([y]/n)? y

cp /pub/jje/ee282/ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025.fasta.gz ./

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $ls 
#should show the ISO_HiFi... file below
#ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025.fasta.gz  output.fa  processed  raw  README.md

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $conda install bioconda::gfatools


srun -A ecoevo282_class --cpus-per-task 16 --pty bash -i
sbatch -A ecoevo282_class --cpus-per-task 16 --pty bash -i


(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-14-23:~/homework4] $hifiasm -l0 -t16 -o hi_output_fi ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025.fasta.gz

#my main assembly going forward:
hi_output_fi.bp.p_ctg.gfa

```

## Assembly assessment 

1. Calculate the N50 of your assembly (this can be done with faSize\+awk\+sort or with bioawk\+awk\+sort) and compare it to the *Drosophila* community reference's contig N50 

```shell
#before you can answer the questions you have to convert the file types from gfa to fa

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $conda install bioconda::gfatools

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $gfatools gfa2fa hi_output_fi.bp.p_ctg.gfa > hi_output_fi.bp.p_ctg.fa
 

```

Print the sequence length and the total length, Sort the genome size from long to short, Calculate the N50, and print the output to out.txt

```shell
#Calculating the N50 for the assembly 

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $bioawk -c fastx '{ tot=length($seq)+tot; print length($seq) } END { print tot }' hi_output_fi.bp.p_ctg.fa \
| sort -k 1,1rn \
| gawk 'NR==1 {tot=$1} NR>1 {cs=$1+cs; print $1 "\t" cs/tot}' \
| gawk '$2 >= 0.5 {print $1; exit}' \
> hi_output_fi.txt

# checking the hi_output_fi.txt file to get the N50 number

(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-l18-05:~/homework4] $gawk '{print $1}' hi_output_fi.txt \
| sort -rn \
| gawk '
NR==1 {tot=$1}
NR>1 {tot+=$1}
{a[NR]=$1}
END {
half=tot/2
cs=0
for(i=1;i<=NR;i++){
cs+=a[i]
if(cs>=half){
print a[i]
exit
}
}
}'

# My N50 value = 21715751
```

The *Drosophila* community’s reference contig N50 had a value of 21.5 Mb, my N50 value for my genome assembly had a N50 value of 21715751 \~ 21.7 Mb. The N50 value for my genome assembly was higher than that of the *Drosophila* community’s.

3. Calculate BUSCO scores of both assemblies and compare them. You can obtain the BUSCOs pipeline from [biconda Links to an external site.](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/busco/README.html)  
   Please install BUSCO in a separate environment.  If you are still having issues you can use  [compleasm Links to an external site.](https://bioconda.github.io/recipes/compleasm/README.html) as an alternative to BUSCO

```shell
#Before starting the BUSCO installation... For ISO assembly: Need to clean the header of the ISO data before using BUSCO (BUSCO doesn't deal with slashes in the header)
(ee282) [sophid2@hpc3-15-16:~/homework4] $gunzip -c /data/homezvol1/sophid2/homework4/ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025.fasta.gz \
| awk 'BEGIN{FS=OFS=""} /^>/{gsub("/","_",$0)} {print}' \
> /data/homezvol1/sophid2/homework4/ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025_cleaned.fasta
```

#Need to copy and paste **all of it** in the nano script for getting the ISO HiFi assembly

```shell

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#SBATCH --job-name=busco_iso
#SBATCH --output=busco_iso_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=busco_iso_%j.err
#SBATCH --account=ecoevo282_class
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00 
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=64G

#Load environment 
source activate busco_env

#Run BUSCO 
busco \
  -i /data/homezvol1/sophid2/homework4/ISO_HiFi_Shukla2025_cleaned.fasta \
  -l diptera_odb10 \
  -o /data/homezvol1/sophid2/homework4/iso_hifi_busco \
  -m genome \
  --cpu 16
```

My answer: 

When comparing the BUSCO scores between the iso-1 *Drosophila melongaster* strain to that of the [dmel-all-chromosome-r6.66.fasta.gz](http://dmel-all-chromosome-r6.66.fasta.gz) file from flybase there are some differences. The first set of differences being in the assembly completeness “C”, for the iso\_hifi\_busco results had a C value of 100.0% versus the C value for the diptera\_odb10 file was 99.9%. I also compared the assembly statistics that also showed significant differences. 

The dmel assembly: 

- Number of scaffolds: 1870  
- Number of contigs: 2442  
- Total length: 143726002  
- Percent gaps: 0.802%  
- Scaffold N50: 25 Mbp  
- Contigs N50: 21 Mbp


The iso\_hifi\_assembly: 

- Number of scaffolds: 324821  
- Number of contigs: 324821  
- Total length: 	5101111620  
- Percent gaps: 0.000%  
- Scaffold N50: 135 kbp  
- Contigs N50: 135 kbp

The assembly statistics show clear differences in all categories when comparing the two assemblies.
